history.period: 9th-10th century (conflicting: some sources say 11th-12th century, Pala King Ramapala or Sena dynasty)
history.summary: CSV town corrected from Purulia to Deulghata (the site lies in Arsha CD block, ~6 km south of Jaypur and ~25 km from Purulia town). Deulghata, literally 'the land of temples', was once a cluster of about 15 temples and small shrines on the bank of the Kangsabati (Kasai) river; today three tall brick rekha deuls with fine stucco decoration survive, taken over by the Archaeological Survey of India (one large deul collapsed a few years ago in a man-made accident). Wikipedia/ASI date them to the 9th-10th century, but other sources (velpu.com, kolkatafusion) attribute them to Pala King Ramapala or the Sena dynasty in the 11th-12th century - dates and patrons conflict. The site's remains are chiefly Jain, though later Hindu use is evident (a small Ganesha image stands inside one deul). The deuls show classic Pala-Sena age stucco work: chaitya and miniature rekha motifs, scrollwork with geese and foliation, and dwarf figures. Coordinates are the published site coordinates from Wikipedia (the map geocoder had no POI for the site).

name: Deulghat Temple
town_description: Deulghata is a tiny riverside village in the Arsha community development block of Purulia district, on the bank of the Kangsabati (Kasai) river about 6 km south of Jaypur and 25 km from Purulia town. It has no tourist infrastructure of its own and is visited as a day trip from Purulia, usually combined with the Ajodhya Hills circuit; the surroundings are farmland dotted with palash and simul trees.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi (nearest functional airport)
travel.road: By road from Purulia town via the Jaypur road, ~25 km; local transport to the village is sparse
